summary: Intermittent client request timeouts during KV-cache warmup under continuous batching
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Dedicated instances are observing intermittent client-side request timeouts (upstream 504s) concentrated during short windows when the serving node's KV cache is warming up after idle periods. The pattern correlates with continuous-batcher activity: spikes in p95/p99 latency and a cluster of timeouts for requests that require cold KV population.

Impact:
- ClipStream Media reports ~2-4% error rate for streaming generation calls during morning traffic ramp for their us-east dedicated pool.
- Affects critical user-facing sync features; customer classifies as P1.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserve id: ded-us-east-028) serving rwd-open-13b-v2 and gpt-neox-20b-quant on NCCL-enabled A100 nodes.
- Ingress through api-gateway (prod us-east).
- Autoscaling disabled for this reserve.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Let a serving node sit idle (~20-40 minutes) for traffic that touches a specific KV-backed prefix
2) Resume burst traffic (short spike of 50 qps for 30s) routed to the same node
3) Continuous batcher begins coalescing requests; some requests reference cached prefixes that are cold
4) Within 10-25s from the spike, we see a cluster of request timeouts (client 504) and p95/p99 token latency spikes

Observed behavior:
- p50 unchanged, p95 and p99 spike up to 1.8–2.5× baseline for 10–30s windows.
- Streaming connections reset for some callers when backend fails to produce tokens within gateway timeout.
- Logs show repeated 'kv-miss; initiating remote fetch' followed by long tail of kernel scheduling in serving-runtime traces.

Expected behavior:
- KV cache warmup should amortize behind batching without causing client-facing timeouts; fallback routing or transient queueing should prevent gateway 504s.

Attachments / quick references:
- Grafana panel snapshots (p95/p99 tokens, batch sizes, continuous-batcher queue depth) attached in ticket thread.
- Sample trace ids: trace-20260310-ue1-08a1, trace-20260310-ue1-08a7.
- Customer recording of failure window (clipstream-prod-20260310-09_12-09_18.mp4).
steps_to_reproduce: Allow node to be idle for 20-40 minutes
Send a short burst of 40-60 qps targeting same node
logs_and_metrics: serving-runtime: repeated 'kv-miss' events followed by remote fetch + kernel wait (timestamps 2026-03-10T09:12:14Z to 09:12:42Z)
continuous-batcher: queue depth rose to 128 and average batch size dropped from 24 to 6 during outage window
api-gateway: upstream timeout 504 for ~3% of requests between 09:12:15-09:12:45 UTC
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KV cache cold misses increase per-request processing time; continuous-batcher reduces batch sizes when many cold keys are present, increasing overhead per request.

Observed that when batch size collapses, kernel scheduling and serialization of remote KV fetches dominate CPU wait leading to head-of-line blocking for subsequent requests in the same micro-batch window.
Verified that affected nodes had KV hit ratio drop from 92% -> 34% at warmup start; warmup completes in ~20s with hit ratio returning to baseline.
Checked autoscaling/placement: no noisy neighbor or GPU OOMs detected; CPU utilization on the host does spike but within headroom.
Reproduced in staging with a synthetic workload that simulates many unique KV prefixes: same p95/p99 spike pattern observed.
temporary_workarounds: Advise customer to enable short-lived warmup traffic (a small steady pre-warming QPS) during business ramp windows
Increase api-gateway upstream timeout to tolerate a 30s tail during scheduled warmup (not ideal long-term)
Temporarily enable a config to prefer routing cold-key requests to a warm pool (manual traffic steering)
Customer applied a 5 qps background warmup job which reduced observed 504s to ~0.2%
long_term_action_items: ENG: Add instrumentation to continuous-batcher to label batches with KV-hit ratios and surface in dashboards (rwd-batcher#417)
RUNTIME: Implement non-blocking KV fetch pipeline to avoid per-request stall inside batch processing (rwd-runtime#834)
PLATFORM: Evaluate small-scale automatic warmup/prefill policy for dedicated pools after idle periods
DOCS: Publish recommended warmup patterns for Dedicated customers and add to on-call runbooks
resolution_notes: Work in progress. Short-term mitigation recommended and accepted by customer: they enabled a low-rate warmup job and increased upstream timeout for morning ramp. Engineering has a targeted plan to reduce blocking KV fetch behavior inside continuous-batcher; PRs opened and tests added. Will schedule follow-up to verify post-deploy metrics for two business ramps.

notes_for_oncall: If seeing similar patterns: check KV hit ratio, batch size distribution, continuous-batcher queue depth. Consider temporary warmup or routing cold-key traffic to a warm replica. Escalate to Runtime if KV fetch latency > 50ms and batch sizes collapse.
